prompt.context_jp: 煙が満ちるエレベーターの狭い箱の中で、妊婦の立花彩乃はうずくまり、破水した腹を必死に抱えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 煙___満ちるエレベーターの狭い箱の中で、妊婦の立花彩乃はうずくまり…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks 'smoke' here.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause ('an elevator that is filled with smoke'), the subject takes が. This is also new information setting the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 煙 the topic of the main clause, but the main-clause topic is 立花彩乃. を would wrongly make 煙 a direct object of 満ちる (an intransitive verb).

contrast_examples.en: a glass with water in it (relative clause → が)

prompt.context_jp: 頭上のワイヤーには音羽尚が宙吊りになり、下の光景を険しい目で見下ろしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭上のワイヤーには音羽尚___宙吊りになり、下の光景を険しい目で見下ろしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Otowa here.

feedback.correct_en: Otowa is being newly introduced into the scene ('there's Otowa suspended above') — classic new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat Otowa as an already-established topic, but this is his entrance into the paragraph. も would imply 'also,' which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: ワイヤーには音羽が吊られていた。
contrast_examples.en: On the wire, Otowa was hanging. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: 音羽はベテラン医師だ。

prompt.context_jp: 「私は手を離せません 急いで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___手を離せません 急いで
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 私 here?

feedback.correct_en: Suzuka is contrasting herself ('as for me, I can't let go — so you go') with the listener. This contrastive-topic usage uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying who can't let go out of a group — not the point. を wouldn't fit a subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は行けないから、あなたが行って。
contrast_examples.en: I can't go, so you go. (contrastive は)
I'll be the one to go. (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: 涼香の口元がかろうじて形作った三文字を、比奈がようやく読み取った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 涼香の口元がかろうじて形作った三文字を、比奈___ようやく読み取った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Hina.

feedback.correct_en: This narrates a specific event — Hina was the one who finally read the lips. New-event subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame Hina as a general topic, flattening the dramatic moment. に doesn't match an agent subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 比奈がようやく気づいた。

contrast_examples.en: Hina is an internist. (defining topic → は)

prompt.context_jp: 「臍帯とは へその緒のことです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 臍帯と___ へその緒のことです
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that defines 'saitai'.

feedback.correct_en: 'XとはYのことです' is a standard definition pattern — 'As for X, it means Y.' The topic marker は is required here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a cleft/identification, not a definition. を can't follow と in this construction.

prompt.context_jp: 「通常 赤ちゃんのあとに へその緒が出てきますが」「へその緒のほうが 先に出てきてしまう状態のことです」
prompt.prompt_jp: へその緒のほう___ 先に出てきてしまう状態のことです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after ほう.

feedback.correct_en: The 〜ほうが pattern contrasts two possibilities and picks one as the exhaustive case ('it's the cord that comes out first'). This exhaustive focus takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the comparison; the point here is identifying which one comes out first. に doesn't fit a subject.

prompt.context_jp: 「待てません 臍帯脱出したら 赤ちゃんは10分と もたない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 臍帯脱出したら 赤ちゃん___10分と もたない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 赤ちゃん.

feedback.correct_en: Kitami states a general claim about the baby's situation ('as for the baby, won't last ten minutes') — topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would focus on identifying who won't last, but the baby is contextually given. も would imply 'the baby also,' which isn't the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「立花さんは私の患者です 扉が開くのを待つべきです！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 立花さん___私の患者です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Tachibana-san.

feedback.correct_en: Otowa makes a statement about Tachibana ('as for Tachibana, she's my patient'). This categorizing claim with a known referent uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like 'It's Tachibana who is my patient,' as if contrasting against others — not the local point. も would require a prior example.

prompt.context_jp: 白金の指示を撥ね付け、音羽は自分の身を釣り上げるロープを手放させた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白金の指示___撥ね付け、音羽は自分の身を釣り上げるロープを手放させた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 指示.

feedback.correct_en: 撥ね付ける ('reject/brush aside') is transitive — its direct object (the instructions) takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as the subject (the instructions did the rejecting). に would mean 'to the instructions,' which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: To obey an order. (に with 従う)

prompt.context_jp: 煙の充満する狭い踊り場で、いくつもの規則を侵すことになる帝王切開が、まさに始まろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: いくつもの規則を侵すことになる帝王切開___、まさに始まろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 帝王切開.

feedback.correct_en: This narrative sentence presents a dramatic event ('a C-section was about to begin') — new-info event subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general topic claim, draining the moment of its dramatic 'about to begin' feel. を doesn't fit an intransitive 始まる.

prompt.context_jp: 全員が同じ患者を見つめ、一つの手術に己の判断を賭けようとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 全員___同じ患者を見つめ、一つの手術に己の判断を賭けようとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 全員.

feedback.correct_en: 全員が means 'every single one of them' — an exhaustive-listing use of が emphasizing the whole group acting together.
feedback.incorrect_en: 全員は would weakly topicalize the group and is awkward here. 全員も would imply 'also everyone,' needing an earlier referent.

prompt.context_jp: 「ダメです ずっと吸ってないですよね あなたが もちません」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた___ もちません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for あなた.

feedback.correct_en: Kitami picks out Suzuka specifically — 'YOU won't hold up.' This exhaustive, pointed focus uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたは would just make 'you' a bland topic, losing the urgency of singling her out. を doesn't fit the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたが倒れたら困る。
contrast_examples.en: If you (specifically) collapse, we're in trouble.

prompt.context_jp: エレベーターの扉が細く開き、担架を運び出す準備が整った。
prompt.prompt_jp: エレベーターの扉___細く開き、担架を運び出す準備が整った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 扉.

feedback.correct_en: The door opening is a new, observed event — a classic new-information が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the door a general topic, which doesn't match this moment-by-moment narration. を doesn't fit an intransitive 開く.

prompt.context_jp: 「心拍回復」「100 超えました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 心拍___ 回復 / 100を超えました
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 心拍 in reporting its sudden recovery?

feedback.correct_en: Reporting a sudden change ('the pulse recovered!') — this is pure new-information. が fits natural event-reporting speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general comment on the pulse. も would mean 'the pulse too,' needing a prior item.

prompt.context_jp: 部屋に足を踏み入れた瞬間、音羽の胸には別の感情がこみ上げてくる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋___足を踏み入れた瞬間
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 部屋.

feedback.correct_en: 踏み入れる takes a goal/destination with に ('stepping INTO the room'). It marks the endpoint of motion.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action, but 踏み入れる focuses on movement into. を can mark a path, not fitting here.

contrast_examples.en: To talk in the room. (location で)

prompt.context_jp: 「私の母は お金もなく ろくな治療も受けられずに 若くして死にました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の母___ お金もなく ろくな治療も受けられずに 若くして死にました
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 私の母.

feedback.correct_en: Otowa opens a personal story about her mother — a topic frame leading into multiple predicates. は marks that topical scope.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow it to new-information focus, as if answering 'who died?' But Otowa is introducing her mother as the subject of a longer narrative. を doesn't fit a subject.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見はマイクを握り直し、隊員一人一人に矢継ぎ早に指示を___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隊員一人一人に矢継ぎ早に指示を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb that collocates with 指示を.

feedback.correct_en: 指示を飛ばす is a set collocation meaning to fire off instructions rapidly — fits 矢継ぎ早に perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 指示を投げる sounds like 'throwing orders carelessly' (closer to 投げる仕事); 指示を渡す isn't idiomatic for issuing orders.

prompt.context_jp: モニターに小さく映る妊婦の姿を、隊員たちは___見つめる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隊員たちは___見つめる。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the expression meaning 'held their breath.'

feedback.correct_en: 息を殺す is the fixed idiom for watching tensely in silence — exactly the tone here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を止める literally means to hold your breath physically; 息を抜く means to relax, the opposite nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「はい ですが 人の___より大事なものなんて この世には ないんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の___より大事なものなんて この世には ないんです
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word that completes this classic MER line.

feedback.correct_en: 人の命 ('a human life') is the signature philosophy of MER — nothing matters more than saving lives.
feedback.incorrect_en: 人の心 ('a person's heart') is a different nuance, about feelings. 人の身 would mean 'a person's body/position,' which doesn't fit the moral weight here.

contrast_examples.en: Life is more important than anything.

prompt.context_jp: 「買いかぶりすぎです 私は政治家に ___ を売ろうと思っただけです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私は政治家に ___ を売ろうと思っただけです
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word that forms 'suck up to.'

feedback.correct_en: こびを売る is the idiom for 'to curry favor / suck up to someone.' Otowa is deflecting praise with self-deprecation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔を売る means 'to make a name for oneself' (quite different). 手を売る isn't idiomatic.

contrast_examples.en: To curry favor with the boss.
To build a reputation in the industry.

prompt.context_jp: 「どんな処分も ___ お受けします」
prompt.prompt_jp: どんな処分も ___ お受けします
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adverb a bureaucrat uses to say 'willingly accept any punishment.'

feedback.correct_en: 甘んじて受ける is a formal set phrase: 'to accept (something unpleasant) without complaint.' Perfect for accepting disciplinary action.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜んで (gladly) would be bizarre for punishment. 仕方なく (reluctantly) breaks the humble, resolute tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 批判を甘んじて受ける。
喜んでお引き受けします。
contrast_examples.en: I'd be happy to take it on. (positive request)

prompt.context_jp: 「天沼先生が おっしゃったことなどは」「どうか ___ にして いただけないでしょうか」
prompt.prompt_jp: どうか ___ にして いただけないでしょうか
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word meaning 'off the record.'

feedback.correct_en: オフレコにする ('to keep off the record') is the exact journalistic/political term Otowa uses when asking Tachibana not to publicize what Amanuma said.
feedback.incorrect_en: 内緒話 means a private secret talk between close people — not the public-record sense. 独り言 means 'talking to oneself.'

contrast_examples.jp: これはオフレコでお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: Please keep this off the record.

prompt.context_jp: 「どうか これを___」
prompt.prompt_jp: どうか これを___
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the humble verb for 'please accept this (envelope).'

feedback.correct_en: お納めいただく is the polite set phrase for asking someone to 'kindly accept' a gift or money — exactly what Otowa, a bureaucrat, must say here.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらっていただく is grammatically awkward (もらう is the giver's humble form). 取っていただく sounds blunt, like 'please take it,' lacking ceremony.

prompt.context_jp: 「音羽先生 本当に ___ ございました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 音羽先生 本当に ___ ございました
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the appropriate thanks for saving a baby's life.

feedback.correct_en: 本当にありがとうございました expresses heartfelt gratitude — Tachibana is thanking Otowa for saving her baby.
feedback.incorrect_en: 申し訳ございません is an apology, which doesn't fit her joy. お疲れさまでした isn't used by patients to doctors in this gratitude sense.

contrast_examples.jp: ありがとうございました。
申し訳ございませんでした。

prompt.context_jp: Opening scene: an elevator filling with smoke.
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening sounds more natural for a scene-setting narrative line?

choices.text: 煙が満ちるエレベーターの狭い箱の中で、妊婦の立花彩乃はうずくまっていた。
煙は満ちるエレベーターの狭い箱の中で、妊婦の立花彩乃がうずくまっていた。

feedback.correct_en: In a relative clause describing the elevator, the subject 煙 takes が; the main-clause topic 彩乃 then takes は. This is the natural news-like narrative flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: Swapping to 煙は inside the relative clause breaks it (は can't normally mark the subject inside a modifying clause), and 彩乃が shifts her out of topic position awkwardly.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降る日に、彼女は出かけた。
contrast_examples.en: On a rainy day, she went out.

prompt.context_jp: Kitami urgently explains the baby won't survive long.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural in Kitami's urgent speech?

choices.text: 臍帯脱出したら 赤ちゃんは10分と もたない
臍帯脱出したら 赤ちゃんが10分と もたない

feedback.correct_en: 赤ちゃんは makes 'the baby' the topic for a general claim ('the baby won't last 10 minutes'). The ~と もたない pattern pairs naturally with a topic subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 赤ちゃんが would narrow the focus to identifying who won't last, which is odd when the baby is already in context.

contrast_examples.en: Who will last three days? (identificational が)

prompt.context_jp: Otowa asserts she is the surgeon in charge.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for her declaration?

choices.text: 私が執刀医です 最後まで責任を持ちます
私は執刀医です 最後まで責任を持ちます

feedback.correct_en: When declaring 'I am the one who's the lead surgeon,' Japanese uses exhaustive-listing が — 私が執刀医です — to assert the identification over anyone else.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は執刀医です sounds like a bland self-introduction ('I'm a surgeon'), not the pointed claim of role that the scene demands.

contrast_examples.en: I am the one in charge.

prompt.context_jp: Otowa visits Tachibana with a formal request.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a bureaucrat's formal visit?

choices.text: 今日は お願いがあって参りました
今日は お願いがあって来ました

feedback.correct_en: 参りました is the humble form of 来ました and matches Otowa's bureaucratic register when making a formal request.
feedback.incorrect_en: 来ました is neutral polite and sounds too casual given the gravity of the request and Otowa's official position.

contrast_examples.en: I have come to pay my respects. (humble)

prompt.context_jp: Tachibana expresses her relief about the baby.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for her heartfelt reaction?

choices.text: この子が 元気に生まれてくれただけで もう 何もいりません
この子は 元気に生まれてくれただけで もう 何もいりません

feedback.correct_en: Inside the modifier-ish subordinate clause '〜が生まれてくれただけで,' が marks the subject naturally. It also conveys the specific event ('this child being born healthy') as the sole thing she needs.
feedback.incorrect_en: この子は would make the baby a general topic for a predicate, but there's no main predicate about the child here — only the embedded event clause. は sounds awkward in this slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来てくれただけで嬉しい。
contrast_examples.en: Just him coming makes me happy.
